kleyo — Ads Report

28 September 2026 · Last 30 days

Meta Ads + Google Ads · Creative insights + Performance

AI

Creative Analysis

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no results

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €6130 spend · 127 results
✅ What's Working
• Comparison statics dominate: 'Static _ Vergelijking #2 - Copy' is the top spender (€1,617) with 38 results at a sustainable €42.56 CPR — the broker-vs-kleyo savings angle clearly resonates with Belgian homeowners.
• Calculation & ticket formats convert efficiently: 'Static _ Berekening #2' (€35.92 CPR, 23 results) and 'Static _ Ticket #1 - Copy' (€34.45 CPR, 9 results) prove that concrete € savings visuals drive leads.
• Thomas Guenter founder/trust creative is the hidden gem: one instance of 'Static _ Thomas Guenter #2 - Copy' hit €17.29 CPR (6 results on just €104 spend) — best efficiency in the entire account, criminally under-spent.
❌ What's Not Working
• 'General Video #1 - Copy' is a budget incinerator: three instances burned €601 combined for exactly 1 total result (€462 CPR on the biggest variant). Whatever was changed from the original killed it.
• 'Static _ Vergelijking #1' is the inferior sibling: both instances combined spent €451 for only 4 results (€85-€195 CPR) while #2 runs at €36-€44. The creative execution matters — #1 should have been cut weeks ago.
• Poll and 'Copy 2' variants underperform across the board: 'Static _ Poll #2 - Copy' averaged €123 CPR, 'Static _ Vergelijking #2 - Copy 2' has a zero-result instance at €104 and €72.69 CPR on the other. Engagement-bait formats don't convert to leads here.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more comparison statics iterating on the #2 framework — test different home price tiers, side-by-side fee breakdowns, and 'what you keep' framing to expand the winning concept.
• Scale the Thomas Guenter / founder trust angle hard — create video and carousel variants; this personal credibility format converts at half the cost of comparison statics but has received 1/8th the budget.
• Build a savings calculator creative series: 'Berekening' proves that showing homeowners their exact € saved at specific price points (€250K, €350K, €500K) is a top-3 conversion driver.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill every 'General Video #1 - Copy' instance immediately — three variants, €601 burned, 1 result. The original works; the copy is poison.
• Kill both 'Static _ Vergelijking #1 - Copy' variants — they've proven at scale that #1 is simply a worse creative than #2. Stop splitting budget.
• Kill 'Static _ Thomas Guenter #2 - Copy 2' — €149 for zero results while 'Copy' (no 2) converts at €17.29. The extra iteration broke it.

Belgium

26 ads · €4201 spend · 55 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Offer/promo statics dominate: 'Static _ Offer #1 - Copy' leads with 2.92x ROAS and lowest CPP (€45.62) — price incentives close the deal.
• Vuelta Split layout is the conversion engine: 'Static _ Vuelta Split #1' (€489 spend) delivers best CPP at €37.60 across 13 purchases at 2.6x ROAS. Split format clearly outsells Full.
• Color variety statics drive volume: 'Static _ Colors #1' pulled 14 purchases as the highest-spend ad at 2.09x ROAS — showing the full range in one frame sells.
❌ What's Not Working
• All Sieben video content is a cash bonfire: 3 videos burned €655 combined for 3 total purchases. 'Video _ Sieben Item #1' alone lost money at 0.89x ROAS on €445. UGC and split video variants got zero purchases.
• HelboF Before&After ads are clickbait traps: 130–163% CTR but zero conversions across €166 combined spend. Curiosity clicks, zero buying intent — you're paying Meta to entertain window shoppers.
• Vuelta Full format consistently underperforms Split: Full variants sit at 1.14–1.74x ROAS vs Split's 2.6x. Plus duplicate Vuelta variants cannibalize each other, with the €185 'Vuelta Split #2' at 0.71x actively losing money.
⬆ Double Down On
• Offer/promo statics across every product line: replicate 'Offer #1 - Copy' format for Ziris, Helbo, and Selva — it's the only format approaching healthy ROAS and has the best CPP in the account.
• Split-layout statics with product detail callouts: Vuelta Split converts at nearly half the CPP of Full — make this the default layout for every product launch and seasonal push.
• Color variety showcases per product family: 'Colors #1' proves showing the range sells — create dedicated color statics for Helbo photochromic, Ziris, and seasonal Selva Snow.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• All Sieben video content immediately — 3 ads, €655, nearly zero return. This creative direction is dead. Don't iterate, abandon.
• HelboF Before&After format — high CTR is masking zero purchase intent. Stop rewarding Meta's algorithm for junk engagement clicks.
• Duplicate underperforming Vuelta variants cannibalizing each other — the 0.71x 'Vuelta Split #2' and 0-purchase 'Vuelta Split #1' (€65) are dragging down the winning versions.

Netherlands

4 ads · €233 spend · 3 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Full-frame format crushes split: 'Static _ Vuelta Full #2' delivers 3.56x ROAS at only €32 CPP — best efficiency in the account.
• High engagement across all creatives — CTRs above 100% suggest strong thumb-stop power with the Vuelta cycling imagery.
• 'Static _ Colors #1' pulls the highest CTR (289%) at minimal spend, signaling colorway variety resonates with NL audiences.
❌ What's Not Working
• Split-frame format is a money pit: 'Static _ Vuelta Split #1' ate €161 (69% of total NL spend) for a miserable 1.4x ROAS and €80 CPP. Split #2 followed the same losing pattern with zero purchases.
• Total NL spend is only €232 across 4 static ads — this market is severely undertested with zero video, zero UGC, and zero product-education creatives.
• No ads leverage NAOS's strongest differentiators (prescription 'op sterkte', photochromic lenses, Belgian quality) — it's all generic product shots.
⬆ Double Down On
• Full-frame product-on-face imagery à la Vuelta Full — the format works, now multiply it across Ziris, Helbo, and seasonal angles.
• Colorway-forward creatives — Colors #1's engagement spike at tiny spend suggests NL shoppers respond to lens/frame variety; build a full series.
• Prescription + photochromic education ads — zero competition from Oakley/Decathlon on 'op sterkte' sportbrillen; own this niche before they do.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill the split-frame format entirely — two data points, same conclusion: it bleeds budget without converting.
• Stop running NL on statics only — you're leaving massive scale on the table by ignoring video and UGC in a market that clearly engages with the brand.

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €2277 spend · 211 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Video content massively outperforms statics — 'Video _ XPL04 MG #1' (ROAS 647.62x), 'Video _ XPL04 KA #1' (ROAS 90.59x), and 'Video _ General #1 ACW' (ROAS 47.18x) are all crushing it with CPPs under €10.
• Retargeting/lifecycle creatives punch above their weight — 'Static _ Hold #1' delivered ROAS 170.57x at a €3.71 CPP on minimal spend, and 'Static _ Repeat #1' hit ROAS 29.47x. These warm audiences convert cheaply.
• The Catalog Carousel format works reliably — 'Catalog Carousel - Espresso Coffee' sustains high spend (€504) while holding strong ROAS (28.69x), proving product-feed-driven creative converts at scale.
❌ What's Not Working
• French-language statics are inefficient — 'Static _ Barista _ FR #1' (CPP €29.38), 'Static _ General _ FR #1' (CPP €42.10), 'Static _ Quality _ FR #2' (CPP €39.09) all have bloated CPPs and mediocre ROAS. The FR creative angle isn't landing.
• The iMessage-style static is a money pit — 'Static _ iMessage #1' spent €120 for 2 purchases at ROAS 2.84x and a €59.98 CPP. Gimmicky format, no substance.
• Several statics got zero purchases — 'Static _ General #1', 'Static _ Never #1', 'Static _ Hold #2' all spent without a single conversion. Dead weight.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more XPL04-style origin/exploration videos — both KA and MG variants dominate across every metric. Create new versions featuring different origins, roast profiles, or farmer stories.
• Scale retargeting creatives for lifecycle segments (Hold, Repeat) — 'Static _ Hold #1' and 'Static _ Repeat #1' prove warm-audience creatives deliver absurd efficiency. Build video versions and fresh angles for these segments.
• Expand Catalog Carousel variants — test different product groupings (subscriptions, single origins, gift sets) to replicate the consistent performance of the Espresso catalog ad.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill 'Static _ iMessage #1' immediately — worst ROAS in the account (2.84x), €60 CPP, zero creative differentiation for a specialty coffee brand.
• Kill all zero-purchase statics — 'Static _ General #1', 'Static _ Never #1', 'Static _ Hold #2' have proven nothing. Stop bleeding budget.
• Stop running underperforming FR statics without iteration — 'Static _ Barista _ FR #1', 'Static _ General _ FR #1', 'Static _ Quality _ FR #2' need a full creative rethink before getting more spend.

Creative Analysis

10 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

10 ads · €865 spend · 10 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Review/social-proof format is the strongest conversion driver — Static _ Review #1 hit 16.42x ROAS and Static _ Review #2 delivered 7.42x in one ad set. Customers trust peer validation for premium beans.
• USvThem comparison angle converts profitably everywhere — Static _ USvThem #1 reached 11.9x ROAS at €39 CPP in one ad set and held 3.39x at higher spend. The 'why we're different' framing resonates with specialty coffee buyers.
• CTRs are strong across nearly all creatives (80-165%), indicating solid hooks and visuals — the bottleneck is post-click conversion, not attention.
❌ What's Not Working
• Static _ Chat #1 is a click trap — 136-164% CTR across two ad sets, €44 total spend, zero purchases. It generates engagement but no buying intent whatsoever.
• Static _ Review #2 at €322 is the biggest spender AND the biggest loser at 0.74x ROAS. The ad set is burning through budget with a €107 CPP on beans that average €19-28 — mathematically impossible to profit.
• Static _ Search #1 is inconsistent — one ad set spent €67 with zero purchases while the other eked out 1.77x ROAS. The search/discovery framing isn't compelling enough to close the sale.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more review/testimonial variations — try specific blend reviews (WILD, ZERO, GOLD), video testimonials, before/after taste comparisons. This is your proven conversion format.
• Expand the USvThem playbook — supermarket beans vs Mister Barish, capsules vs fresh espresso, generic machines vs expert-curated picks. Comparison framing is your second strongest angle.
• Create urgency and bundle-driven creatives that leverage free shipping above €75 — this USP is untapped and could boost AOV while giving ads a concrete CTA beyond 'buy coffee.'
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Pause Static _ Chat #1 immediately — both ad sets combined spent €44 with zero conversions. High CTR with no purchases means the creative attracts curiosity clickers, not buyers.
• Pause the high-spend Static _ Review #2 ad set (€322, 0.74x) — it has burned €322 returning only €238. The same creative works at low spend in another ad set, so the creative isn't dead but this audience/scaling is.
• Stop running Static _ Search #1 in the zero-purchase ad set (€67 wasted) — the search/discovery concept needs a complete rethink before more budget goes in.

Action List — Creative Team
1 ⬆ scale Static _ Review #1 16.42x ROAS at tiny spend — needs real budget now
2 ⬆ scale Static _ USvThem #1 11.9x ROAS ad set is the top performer
3 ⏸ pause Static _ Review #2 €322 at 0.74x ROAS is bleeding money
4 ⏸ pause Static _ Chat #1 €44 spent, zero purchases, no conversion signal
5 ⏸ pause Static _ Search #1 €67 ad set has zero purchases — dead
6 ✏️ create Static _ Review #3 — Blend-Specific Testimonial Feature a real customer reviewing a named blend (WILD or ZERO) with tasting notes and star rating. Reviews convert — give them product specificity.
7 ✏️ create Video _ USvThem — Supermarket vs Mister Barish Side-by-side video showing supermarket beans vs freshly roasted Mister Barish pour. Visual proof of quality difference in motion unlocks new placements and scale.
8 ✏️ create Static _ Bundle Builder — Free Shipping Hook Show 3 bags of different blends totaling €75+ with a 'FREE SHIPPING' badge. Leverage untapped USP to drive AOV and give a reason to buy now.
9 ✏️ create Static _ Expert Pick — Machine + Beans Pairing Position Mister Barish as the expert: 'We tested 47 machines. Pair the Sage Barista Express with our GOLD blend.' Combines machine + bean sale in one creative.
10 ✏️ create UGC _ Unboxing — Morning Ritual Lo-fi phone-shot style: someone opens a Mister Barish delivery, grinds PURE beans, pulls a shot. Authentic format to complement polished static winners.
11 🧪 test Rainforest Alliance certification as primary headline hook Currently buried — test whether sustainability-forward messaging lifts conversion among eco-conscious Belgian buyers.
12 🧪 test Workplace/office angle vs home barista angle Mister Barish serves both segments but all current ads feel home-focused. Test dedicated B2B-style creative targeting office managers.
13 🧪 test Review format as carousel — multiple blends in one ad Review #1 and #2 prove the format. Test a carousel where each card is a different blend review to increase engagement time and cross-sell.
14 🧪 test Price-anchoring hook — cost per cup vs café Show that a €24 bag makes 50+ espressos at €0.48/cup vs €3.50 at a café. Rational justification for premium pricing.

Belgium

12 ads · €859 spend · 0 results
✅ What's Working
• Exceptionally high CTRs across the board — 'Static _ General #1' (142.25%) and 'Static _ Myth #2' (136.50%) prove the creative hooks are grabbing attention.
• Three distinct angles (Myth, Us vs Them, General) all generate strong click engagement, suggesting brand/product interest exists in the Belgian market.
• 'Us vs Them' competitive framing resonates — 'Static _ USvsTHEM #1' pulled 89.52% CTR at €195 spend, showing appetite for comparison content.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero conversions across ALL 12 ads on €860 total spend — this is a full-funnel failure, not a creative problem. Every click is dying post-click.
• Static-only creative library with no video, no carousel, no lead form native ads — you're leaving Belgium's highest-converting formats untouched.
• Duplicate ad names across ad sets ('Static _ Myth #1', 'Static _ USvsTHEM #2', etc.) suggest poor campaign structure — budget is fragmenting instead of consolidating learners.
⬆ Double Down On
• Fix the post-click experience IMMEDIATELY — landing page, offer, or conversion event is broken. High CTR + zero results = the ads work but the funnel doesn't.
• Shift to Meta native lead forms (instant forms) to bypass the broken landing page and capture intent directly — especially for the Myth and Us vs Them angles that are generating clicks.
• Produce video creative — Belgium's Meta auction rewards video with cheaper CPMs; use the existing static concepts (myth-busting, comparisons) as storyboard templates for 15-30s clips.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop all traffic to the current landing page until conversion tracking is verified and the page is audited — you're burning cash on a broken funnel.
• Kill the fragmented duplicate ad structure — consolidate identical creatives into single ad sets to give Meta's algorithm enough data to optimize.
• Stop running static-only campaigns in a market where you have zero proof of static-to-conversion performance.

Creative Analysis

12 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no results

🇧🇪

Belgium

12 ads · €1345 spend · 184 results
✅ What's Working
• Naoshima #2 is the clear winner: 62 results at €5.62 CPR on €348 spend — best efficiency-at-scale in the set.
• Sommerfeld variants (#2 and #3) deliver consistent sub-€7 CPRs, proving that creative theme resonates with the affluent coastal audience.
• Static imagery works for this category — all top performers are statics, confirming that architectural photography carries enough stopping power for lead-gen.
❌ What's Not Working
• Bauhaus is oversaturated with 6 variants eating budget unevenly — #5 bleeds at €16.48 CPR (3x worse than Naoshima #2), while #4 and #3 burned €16 combined with zero results.
• Low-spend ads (Naoshima #1, #3, Sommerfeld #1) never got a fair auction signal — Meta's algorithm starved them because the ad set has too many creatives competing for limited budget.
• No ROAS tracking on any ad makes it impossible to connect leads to revenue — a critical blind spot for properties worth six-to-seven figures.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more Naoshima-style creatives: whatever visual angle #2 uses (likely clean interiors or sweeping coastal context), it converts at nearly half the cost of the average Bauhaus ad.
• Lean into Sommerfeld's visual language with fresh angles — two of three variants perform, so the concept has legs; test new compositions and copy hooks.
• Introduce motion formats (video walkthroughs, animated reveals) to complement proven static themes — the entire account runs zero video, leaving a massive creative gap untested.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill Bauhaus #5 immediately — €99 spent at €16.48 CPR is nearly 3x worse than the account's best performers. No justification to keep spending.
• Consolidate the Bauhaus variant bloat: 6 versions fragment learning. Keep #2 and #1, axe the rest.
• Stop running campaigns without ROAS/value tracking — at this price point, one closed deal covers months of ad spend, and you're blind to it.

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no results

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €2203 spend · 71 results
✅ What's Working
• B2B ads generate 100% of all results — top 3 (Boost #2, 4 Momenten #1, Açai Koffiebar) deliver 52 results at €21–26 CPR, proving HoReCa targeting is the account's engine.
• Practical, benefit-driven B2B messaging dominates — use-case framing (4 Momenten), category targeting (Koffiebar), and operational ease (Boost) consistently convert, while abstract angles like Geen excuus collapse.
• B2B Snel #2 quietly posted the best CPR in the account at €15.98 on minimal spend — signals a speed/convenience angle worth feeding.
❌ What's Not Working
• Consumer ads are a total zero — 8 creatives, €275+ spent, literally 0 results across Deinze, Watersportbaan, Notes, Carrousel, Bowl, Organic, and Wekker. No retailer CTA, no endorser leverage, no reason for a consumer to act.
• Abstract motivational concepts bomb even in B2B — Geen excuus #1 burned €107 for a single result despite the highest CTR in the set; high curiosity clicks, zero intent.
• The account is 100% static creative — no video, no motion, no UGC. Leaving massive engagement and scroll-stop potential on the table in a visual product category.
⬆ Double Down On
• B2B practical messaging: replicate the Boost, 4 Momenten, and Koffiebar frameworks with new variants — operational ease, use-case moments, and category-specific targeting are proven converters.
• Rebuild consumer campaigns from scratch around retail partners (Bio-Planet, Delhaize) and Belgian endorsers (Bekkari, Gruyaert) — current consumer ads have no path-to-purchase and no trust signals.
• Introduce video creative in B2B: 15-second prep demos, bowl-building footage, and café testimonials to break through the all-static fatigue.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Every current consumer static ad — zero results across the board; stop burning budget on directionless lifestyle images with no CTA or retail anchor.
• The entire 'Geen excuus' concept (both #1 and #2) — motivational copy doesn't convert in B2B or anywhere; €114 wasted for 1 result combined.
• Location-specific consumer targeting (Deinze, Watersportbaan) — hyper-local without a webshop or store-specific CTA is pointless spend.

✅ What's Working
• "Instagram post: Neem een kijkje online!..." is the standout performer at 10.26x ROAS — clear CTA and direct shopping language converts.
• "Instagram Post" (€90 spend) generated 2 purchases at 2.35x ROAS — proves product-forward content can drive sales when the creative is right.
• Ads with explicit shopping intent language ("Neem een kijkje online") dramatically outperform vague or emoji-only posts.
❌ What's Not Working
• 7 out of 10 ads generated zero purchases despite €395+ combined spend — most creatives are engagement traps with no conversion path.
• Generic boosted posts like "Instagram-bericht" (€125), "Instagram-bericht: ❤️" (€121), and "Instagram-bericht: www.clothingdemasure.be" (€47) burn budget with no sales — lazy creative, no hook, no CTA.
• The account is boosting organic Instagram posts instead of building purpose-built conversion ads — this is the core problem.
⬆ Double Down On
• CTA-driven creatives with explicit shopping language ("Bekijk online", "Shop nu") — the only formula that's actually converting.
• Product-specific ads showing individual items with pricing — move away from generic brand awareness posts toward direct-response.
• Dutch-language, benefit-led copy that tells the customer exactly what to do next — replicate the "Neem een kijkje online" structure across new products.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop boosting random Instagram posts with no CTA, no product focus, and no conversion intent — this is not a growth strategy, it's a budget incinerator.
• Kill all ads that have spent €40+ with zero purchases immediately — "Instagram-bericht" (€125), "Instagram-bericht: ❤️" (€121), "Instagram-bericht: www.clothingdemasure.be" (€47), "Instagram Post" (€45).
• Stop using URLs as ad copy ("www.clothingdemasure.be") — it screams amateur and adds zero persuasion.

Creative Analysis

2 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no results

🇧🇪

Belgium

2 ads · €91 spend · 0 results
✅ What's Working
• Extremely high CTRs on both 120239394435940631 (109.60%) and 120239393986810631 (145.99%) suggest the creative hooks are grabbing attention and generating clicks — the ads themselves are not the bottleneck.
• Low-spend testing approach is smart for a niche B2B workwear market in Belgium — prevents big cash burns while learning.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero results across both ads despite €90 total spend and sky-high CTRs — this screams broken conversion tracking, wrong campaign objective (likely traffic/engagement instead of conversions), or a landing page that kills intent on arrival.
• CTRs above 100% are abnormal and suggest campaigns are optimized for engagement or all-clicks, not purchase/lead events — meaning Meta is finding clickers, not buyers.
• Budget is critically low at €90/month total — insufficient to exit learning phase for any conversion-optimized campaign in Belgium's B2B workwear market.
⬆ Double Down On
• Fix the funnel first: verify Pixel/CAPI fires correctly on lead or purchase events, then relaunch with Conversion objective targeting leads or quote requests — the click demand clearly exists.
• Lean into the high-CTR creative style (whatever is generating those clicks) but pair it with a clear B2B CTA: 'Vraag een offerte aan' (request a quote), free sample kits, or bulk pricing hooks.
• Produce Dutch-language (Belgian Dutch) creative specifically addressing pain points of facility managers, HR buyers, and procurement teams — the actual decision-makers in workwear purchasing.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running any campaign not optimized for conversions or leads — traffic and engagement objectives are burning budget without pipeline.
• Stop spending below €15/day per ad set — you will never exit Meta's learning phase and data will remain useless.

Belgium

30 ads · €5958 spend · 40 results
✅ What's Working
• "Static _ Rip #1" is the clear winner: 17 results at €48 CPR on €816 spend — best efficiency and volume in the account.
• "Static _ Notes #1" (€160 variant) delivers €53 CPR, proving informational/note-style creatives convert well in this market.
• Copy variants outperform originals: "Static _ Business #1 - Copy" generated 13 results while original "Static _ Business #1" burned €1,672 for zero.
❌ What's Not Working
• Video creatives are a dead zone: all four Concierge/Call videos (€247 combined) produced zero results. The format is not landing.
• "Static _ Business #1" original is the single biggest waste — €1,672 spent with literally zero results. Should have been killed weeks ago.
• Multiple statics with high CTR but zero conversions ("Static _ BefoAfter #1" at 341% CTR, "Static _ Business #2" at 259% CTR) — traffic is clicking but not converting, pointing to a landing page or offer mismatch.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more "Rip" style creatives — the torn/disrupted visual treatment is clearly pattern-interrupting AND converting. Test new angles with this format.
• Lean into note/handwritten style statics — "Static _ Notes #1" converts at €53 CPR. This informal, personal aesthetic resonates.
• Create more review/social proof statics — "Static _ Review #1 - Copy" at €69.55 CPR shows promise. Stack testimonials and credibility signals.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Concierge video variants immediately — four versions, zero results, zero signal of life.
• Kill the original "Static _ Business #1" — €1,672 down the drain. The Copy version works; the original does not.
• Stop launching new creatives without fixing the conversion funnel — too many ads show strong CTR with zero results, suggesting the post-click experience is broken.

Zabra — Ads Report

28 September 2026 · Last 30 days

Meta Ads + Google Ads · Creative insights + Performance

AI

Creative Analysis

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no results

🌐

Other

30 ads · €9380 spend · 142 results
✅ What's Working
• Native/interior formats crushing it — "stokerie_int_v1_rem - native" delivers €23.10 CPR with 543% CTR, and "Vottem_animatie" at €24.71 CPR is the second cheapest lead across the portfolio.
• Video formats for certain projects outperform static — "west_video" pulls €38.33 CPR beating "west_ext" at €57.02, and "Brugge_penthouse" leads volume with 26 results at solid €37.22 CPR.
• Animation and native creative styles consistently beat polished/produced content — the scrappier, more organic formats (native, animatie, reel-style) tend to win on efficiency.
❌ What's Not Working
• Charleroi is a money pit — "Charleroi_native" burns €700 for 3 results (€233 CPR) and "Charleroi_te-huur" spent €289 for 1 result at €289 CPR. Market or creative misfire, either way it's bleeding.
• Big-budget produced content without clear hooks is dying — "wildebeek_realisatie_video" (€150 CPR), "wildebeek_drink - v2" (€168 CPR), and "ODD Wildenbeek 1/10/26" (€226 for ZERO results) show Wildebeek creative needs a full reset.
• Slideshows and overly generic CTAs stall — "georges_slideshow" spent €153 with zero results, suggesting the format doesn't create enough urgency or differentiation.
⬆ Double Down On
• Native interior/lifestyle formats across ALL projects — the stokerie native style is the blueprint. Replicate that raw, scroll-stopping interior walkthrough for Vottem, West, Brugge, and Georges.
• Short-form animation and motion graphics — Vottem_animatie proves animated explainers convert cheaply (€24.71 CPR). Create project-specific animations for every active development.
• Penthouse/premium unit spotlights — Brugge_penthouse shows that focusing on a hero unit type drives volume. Identify the hero unit in each project and build dedicated ads around it.
🛑 Kill or Rethink

Belgium

30 ads · €3938 spend · 109 results
✅ What's Working
• Original (non-V2) Doorstromer creatives dominate: "Doorstromer #1 - Copy" delivers 53 results at €15.10 CPR and "Doorstromer #2 - Copy" hits €11.84 CPR — best in account.
• Alleenstaand #2 is a reliable second pillar with 29 results at €20.25 CPR on €587 spend — the only other ad with real volume and efficiency.
• Original creative style consistently outperforms V2 reworks across every segment: lower CTR but dramatically better conversion rates, suggesting V2 versions are engagement traps that don't convert.
❌ What's Not Working
• V2 versions are a catastrophe across the board: "Doorstromer V2 #1" burned €1,257 at €125.65 CPR (8x worse than its original), "General V2 #1" spent €258 for 1 result, and "Algemeen #2 V2" spent €109 for zero results.
• ODD and Jong Koppel segments show sky-high CTRs (300%+) but near-zero conversions — classic clickbait pattern with no downstream intent.
• The account is bleeding budget on underperformers: €1,950+ spent on ads with CPR above €45 or zero results, while the two best performers share only €836 combined.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more original-style Doorstromer creatives — this segment converts best and the two "-Copy" variants prove the angle scales. Test new hooks, offers, and layouts within this winning framework.
• Expand Alleenstaand creative variations using the #2 original style as the template — it's proven at scale and the segment clearly has intent.
• Build dedicated conversion-focused creatives for underserved segments (Jong Koppel, Algemeen) using the visual and copy style of the original winners, not the V2 treatment.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill every V2 creative immediately — they universally destroy CPR and have burned €1,930+ with almost nothing to show. The V2 redesign direction is objectively worse.
• Stop spending on ODD segment until you understand why 300%+ CTR produces virtually zero conversions — likely a landing page or targeting mismatch.
• Stop spreading budget across 20 ads — consolidate into the 3-4 proven winners and reallocate saved budget to scaling them.

✅ What's Working
• "VERANDAS PUB CONVERTION - Copie" delivers the lowest cost/result (€5.55) and highest CTR (342%) — veranda-specific messaging clearly resonates with this audience.
• "CARPORTS" is the only ad with meaningful spend (€49) and still converts at a manageable €16.36/result — carport demand is real in this market.
• Conversion-optimized campaigns (PUB CONVERTION) paired with specific product categories outperform generic approaches.
❌ What's Not Working
• "PERGOLAS - PUB CONVERTIONS" burns €14 with sky-high CTR (264%) but zero conversions — massive disconnect between click interest and landing page or offer.
• "PVC- PER - PUB CONVERTION" is completely dead: €1 spend, 0% CTR, zero results — likely audience or creative failure at the impression level.
• Overall budget is dangerously thin (€75 total) — no ad has enough data for confident optimization, leaving the account flying blind.
⬆ Double Down On
• Veranda-specific conversion ads — replicate the "VERANDAS PUB CONVERTION - Copie" formula with fresh creative variations to validate the €5.55 CPR at higher spend.
• Carport content with stronger post-click experience — the demand is proven, now tighten the funnel to push cost/result below €10.
• Product-specific segmentation over bundled messaging — single-product ads (verandas, carports) outperform mixed-category ads (PVC-PER) every time in this account.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• "PVC- PER - PUB CONVERTION" — zero engagement at any level; this creative/audience combo is DOA.
• Stop spreading €75 across four campaigns — consolidate budget behind proven winners to exit learning phase faster.
• Stop duplicating campaign names with typos (CONVERTIONS vs CONVERTION) — clean up naming conventions to enable proper tracking.

• Carousel format underperforms static: "Carrousel | Wedstrijd" spent €44 for 1 result (€43.90 CPR) vs. the static visual version at €12.60 — same concept, 7x worse efficiency.
• "Gif | Wedstrijd" and "Video" got almost no delivery, suggesting Meta's algorithm deprioritized them quickly against stronger variants.
⬆ Double Down On
• Static image + contest mechanic — it's your proven formula. Produce more visual variations of Wedstrijd-style campaigns with fresh prizes or seasonal hooks.
• Location-specific action CTAs like the Zwin cleanup ad — tie content to recognizable West Flanders landmarks with a clear reason to engage.
• Simple, bold single-image creatives — every top performer is a static visual. Lean into thumb-stopping design over complex formats.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill the IZWVL persona campaign entirely. Two ads, €115 spent, 1 result. The ambassador/testimonial angle is not landing.
• Stop running carousel and GIF variants of contests — the static visual dominates. Don't split budget into weaker formats.

🌐

Other

10 ads · €429 spend · 0 results
✅ What's Working
• Store opening content drives massive engagement — 'Van harte welkom in onze nieuwe winkel in Lokeren' hit 999% CTR and 'Feestelijke opening' hit 424% CTR, proving local community content resonates.
• Product storytelling with brand authority works — 'PrimaDonna San Angel' (442% CTR) and 'Fashion meets verfijning' (384% CTR) show that naming premium brands and describing fabrics/details hooks the audience.
• Instagram-native formats outperform on efficiency — 'Instagram-bericht: Welkom in onze winkel' delivered 601% CTR on only €25 spend, suggesting organic-feeling creative wins.
❌ What's Not Working
• ZERO conversions across every single ad — €430 total spend with literally 0 tracked results. This screams broken pixel, wrong campaign objective (likely boosted posts/engagement instead of conversions), or no purchase event firing. This is the #1 problem.
• Boosted post strategy is burning cash — every ad name starts with 'Bericht' or 'Instagram-bericht' or 'Evenement', confirming these are boosted organic posts, not proper conversion-optimized campaigns. Engagement ≠ revenue.
• No clear CTA or offer structure in any ad — 'Wit of zwart?' and 'Coole, comfy styles' read like social captions, not direct response ads. No urgency, no offer, no reason to buy now.
⬆ Double Down On
• Local store opening content repackaged into conversion campaigns — the Lokeren opening content clearly resonates; rebuild it with proper purchase objectives, a grand opening offer, and a shop-now CTA.
• Premium brand showcase ads (PrimaDonna, etc.) rebuilt as catalog/collection ads with conversion objectives and product links — the audience responds to named brands and fabric storytelling.
• Instagram-first creative formats (Reels, Stories) with organic feel but proper conversion tracking — the Instagram posts already outperform on engagement efficiency, now add commerce infrastructure.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop boosting posts immediately — every euro spent on engagement objectives with no conversion tracking is wasted. Rebuild as proper Sales/Conversion campaigns.
• Kill the vague lifestyle captions with no CTA — 'Coole, comfy styles' and 'We starten de week met heel veel nieuwe reeksen' say nothing actionable. No offer = no conversion.
